study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To develop hierarchical Bayesian normative models that explicitly model site effects and compare them against common harmonization approaches (e.g., ComBat, regressing out site) for predicting cortical thickness from age/sex; evaluate whether site effects are removed while preserving clinically useful signal (ASD vs controls).

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study uses healthy controls and autism participants from ABIDE for model development, testing, and clinical application.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: "We used data of 570 healthy individuals from the ABIDE (autism brain imaging data exchange) data set ... we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set"

rci2_hc_n.reason: Explicitly reported number of controls used for development and testing.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: "For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models"

rci3_hc_age.answer: mean NR; sd NR; min NR; max NR
rci3_hc_age.reason: Overall age summary statistics for healthy controls are not reported in extractable text. Figure/Table references show distributions and site-wise ranges but no aggregated numeric values are provided in text.
rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: "An overview of the distribution of age and sex ... can be found in Fig. 2"; "An overview of site-specific data is provided in Table 1"

rci4_hc_sex.reason: Text reports 569 controls with 470 males; female count inferred as 569-470=99 and percentages computed.
rci4_hc_sex.supporting_text: "we used 569 controls ... out of which 470 were male"

rci5_imaging_modality.reason: ABIDE structural MRI was used and cortical thickness was the imaging-derived measure modeled.
rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: "The consortium provides a publicly available structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data set ... For the current study, we focused on cortical thickness measures ..."

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: "cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikan–Killiany atlas"

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer standard pipeline (Desikan–Killiany atlas) via Preprocessed Connectomes Project; extraction from aparc.stats; outlier detection using ±2 IQR; left–right hemisphere averaging; region-wise standardization based on training set.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: Methods section describes FreeSurfer/Desikan–Killiany processing from the Preprocessed Connectomes Project, followed by explicit QC/outlier handling, hemisphere averaging, and standardization before modeling.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: "... FreeSurfer standard pipeline (Desikan-Kiliany Atlas) as part of the Preprocessed Connectomes Project ... For the current study, we focused on cortical thickness measures ... of the Desikan Killiany atlas ..."; "Measures of cortical thickness were extracted from the aparc.stats files ... scanned for outliers ... above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges ... removal of 1055 out of 162905 data points ... After this step, the values of right and left hemisphere ... were averaged ..."; "... sets were standardized region-wise based on location and scale parameters of the training set."

rci8_quality_checking.detail: Automated outlier detection (±2 IQR) per region/hemisphere; removed 1055/162,905 data points (reported 0.006%); used only complete pairs per region after standardization.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: "Measures ... were scanned for outliers ... above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges ... This leads to the removal of 1055 out of 162905 data points (0.006%) ... After this step, the values of right and left hemisphere ... were averaged ... For the model estimation process only complete pairs of observations (per region) were used."

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Hierarchical Bayesian regression with site modeled as random effects; evaluated residual site effects via ANOVA on z-scores; compared against batch-removal approaches (regressing out site; ComBat and modified ComBat).
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: "... we developed and compared two versions of a hierarchical Bayesian models that include site as a predictor ... site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ..."; "Using ANOVAs with site as predictor indicates that site cannot be predicted from the z-scores ..."; "The harmonization procedures include ... regressing out site ... using ComBat ... modified ComBat ..."

nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: "we developed and compared two versions of a hierarchical Bayesian models that include site as a predictor"

nm2_modeling_method.answer: Hierarchical Bayesian regression (linear mixed model; Gaussian Process term for age)
nm2_modeling_method.reason: Two hierarchical Bayesian variants are presented: a linear mixed model (HBLM) with site random effects and a non-linear model with a Gaussian Process term for age (HBGPM).
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: "... hierarchical Bayesian Linear Model, HBLM ... a Gaussian Process for age is added ... ('Hierarchical Bayesian Gaussian Process Model, HBGPM')"

nm3_software_tool.reason: Implementation and preprocessing details specify Stan for Bayesian inference and R for preprocessing/ComBat.
nm3_software_tool.supporting_text: "R ... was used for preprocessing ... and for preprocessing the data with ComBat ..."; "... implemented in Stan ... and analyzed in R using the package rstan"

nm4_response_variable.answer: Cortical thickness (Desikan–Killiany parcellation; 34 bilateral ROIs; global average thickness also used)
nm4_response_variable.reason: Explicitly states focus on cortical thickness for 34 bilateral regions (averaged) and average cortical thickness.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: "we focused on cortical thickness measures of the 34 bilateral regions (averaged between left and right hemisphere) of the Desikan Killiany atlas ... and the average cortical thickness across all 34 regions"

nm5_predictor_variables.reason: Model specification discusses association between age, sex, and cortical thickness with site modeled in a hierarchical structure.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: "... normative models describing the association between age, sex, and cortical thickness measures ..."; "The ability of the model to deal with site effects is obtained by introducing a random effect for site ..."

nm6_predictor_effects.answer: Age/Sex = fixed; Site = random (hierarchical); Age modeled nonlinearly via GP in HBGPM
nm6_predictor_effects.reason: Site is introduced as a random effect; β are fixed effects; non-linear GP term for age used in HBGPM.
nm6_predictor_effects.supporting_text: "... introducing a random effect for site ... prediction ... is a combination of fixed and varying effects ..."; "For the non-linear models, we assume γ is a Gaussian Process ... to allow for non-linear dependencies ..."

nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: Nuisance structure (site effects; age nonlinearity) is handled via hierarchical random effects for site and GP for age. Residual site effects in z-scores are tested and largely absent/reduced.
nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: "site is modeled hierarchically, resulting in a random effect for site ..."; "Using ANOVAs with site as predictor indicates that site cannot be predicted from the z-scores ..."

nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: Model performance metrics are reported on the training set in addition to the held-out test set (same domain).
nm8_nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: "... training set ... and test set ..." with metrics reported across both sets (e.g., EV, MSLL, ρ).

nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The control cohort was split into 70/30 train/test with a within-site split; models trained on training set and evaluated on held-out test set.
nm9_nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: "split the healthy control data set into a training set (70% ... n=389) and a test set (30% ... n=166) ... within-site-split"; "Both hierarchical Bayesian models were trained and tested in a within-site split"

nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: Models trained on controls were applied to an independent clinical ASD subset from the same ABIDE dataset to assess preservation of clinical signal; no external dataset/sites were used.
nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: "we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set"; "applied ... to the patient data set ... compared ... atypical z-values"

caa1_clinical_dataset.reason: Clinical application used autism participants from the same ABIDE dataset.
caa1_clinical_dataset.supporting_text: "we applied the hierarchical Bayesian models to 482 individuals with autism from the same data set"

caa2_diseases_studied.reason: The clinical group is autism spectrum disorder.

caa4_clinical_groups_age.supporting_text: "An overview of the distribution of age and sex ... can be found in Fig. 2"

caa5_clinical_groups_sex.reason: Text reports 482 autism participants with 430 males; female count inferred (482-430=52) and percentages computed.
caa5_clinical_groups_sex.supporting_text: "... 482 individuals with autism ... out of which 430 were male"

caa6_deviation_metric.reason: Deviation quantified as individual-level z-scores from the normative model; atypical defined at ±1.96 and used to compare ASD vs controls.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: "Finally, each individual's z-score of deviation can be calculated ..."; "We define a z-score of ± 1.96 ... as atypical value ... the average percentage of individuals with extreme z-scores is 5.7% ..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of extreme deviation prevalence (|z|≥1.96) between ASD and control test sets by region; also ANOVA tests to assess residual site effects in z-scores.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Hierarchical Bayesian models outperformed harmonization baselines and produced z-scores with little to no residual site effects while preserving higher prevalence of atypical deviations in ASD vs controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: HBLM/HBGPM retained substantially more predictive variance (57%/65%) than harmonization models and achieved better fit metrics (ρ, SRMSE, EV, MSLL). Z-scores showed no residual site effects in training and reduced effects in test sets; atypical z-score prevalence ~5.5–5.7% in controls vs ~7.2–7.8% in ASD.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: (1) High computational cost for GP variant; (2) Evaluation used within-site split—generalization to entirely new sites left for future work; (3) Does not model correlations between different brain measures.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: "... Gaussian Process ... amounted to 25 hours per model per region ..."; "... between-site split and the model at its current state only allow generalizations to a test set which includes individuals from the same sites as the training set ... generalizing ... to new sites is an important additional goal"; "this approach does not account for correlations between different brain measures"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Clinical application compares ASD vs controls using region-wise counts of atypical z-scores (|z|≥1.96); results illustrate preserved clinical signal despite site-effect handling.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: ABIDE processing used FreeSurfer/Desikan–Killiany via the Preprocessed Connectomes Project; modeling used 34 bilateral ROIs plus global thickness. Controls were split 70/30 within-site (n=389/166). Supplement notes that some sample sizes vary for certain harmonization models (e.g., ComBat-GAM requires complete cases per 35 regions), but the main normative modeling results used the reported control and ASD counts.
